subject: EdgeFin benchmarking: performance/SLO qualification & methodology exchange
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@edgefin.com>, Noah Klein <noah.k@edgefin.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: EdgeFin benchmarking: performance/SLO qualification & methodology exchange

Hi Samir / Noah 14

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a reproducible benchmark run scheduled:

Recap of requirements you shared:
- Latency targets: p95 <= 120ms for typical 512-token responses (goal); p99 target TBD for tail analysis.
- Throughput: baseline target ~200 qps for your steady-state load.
- Concurrency: 40-60 concurrent streams (clients maintain streaming connections).
- Streaming: streaming required (server-side chunked output) with max tokens per response ~512, average 220.
- Model: want to validate both the gen-1.1 and gen-1.2 family variants (we can map to Redwood model IDs).

Open items we need from you to finalize the benchmark plan:
1) A shareable prompt set/eval documents (representative prompts and expected behaviors).
2) Confirmation of test dataset size and distribution (how many warm-up requests vs steady-state).
3) Any special tokenization/stop-sequence semantics we should reproduce.
4) Preferred measurement definitions (how you want latency percentiles, throughput windowing, warm-up duration).

What Redwood will provide:
- Our eval harness (measurement definitions, warm-up/steady-state tooling, and scripts) and recommended prompt-set format (jsonl).
- A proposed benchmark run plan with warm-up, steady-state windows, and required telemetry to collect (GPU utilization, per-request timings, network latency).
- Timeline: if we get the prompt set + spec this week, we can schedule a bench run the week of Oct 5 and share a detailed report by Oct 9.

Next steps / ask:
- Samir/Noah: please send the prompt-set + any internal benchmark spec you have. If attachments are sensitive, a Drive link works.
- Vivek / Dylan: I19m looping you in to review the measurement definitions and make sure the harness captures KV-cache warm-up and streaming semantics.

Thanks 14 happy to hop on a quick 30m sync if helpful.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@edgefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Noah Klein <noah.k@edgefin.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeFin benchmarking: performance/SLO qualification & methodology exchange

Hi Marissa 14

Appreciate the recap. Attaching our baseline spec and prompt set for the initial run: edgefin-benchmark-specs.xlsx and edgefin-prompt-set-v1.jsonl. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Latency: p95 <= 120ms is our goal for 512-token responses, p99 should be captured for SLA engineering but we don19t expect p99 to be under 120ms.
- Throughput: 200 qps is our target, with burst to 350 for peak events.
- Concurrency: clients open persistent streaming connections (approx 50 concurrent). We measure concurrency by active outstanding streams, not queued requests.
- Streaming: we stream partial tokens as they arrive. We also send early-cancel sometimes 14 harness should record partial responses as successful if partial meets criteria.

Notes on dataset: prompt-set v1 contains 2.5k prompts across short/medium/long categories; we19d like a 5-minute warm-up then 15-minute steady-state window.

We19ve shared the files via Drive as well: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1EdgeFinBenchmark (you should have access).

We19re aiming for a benchmark run the week of Oct 5. Let us know what infra keys / endpoint you need for the run.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of Platform Engineering
EdgeFin
samir.patel@edgefin.com

Attachments: edgefin-benchmark-specs.xlsx, edgefin-prompt-set-v1.jsonl

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@edgefin.com>, Noah Klein <noah.k@edgefin.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeFin benchmarking: performance/SLO qualification & methodology exchange

Thanks Samir 14 got the Drive link and the attachments. I attached the Redwood eval harness (redwood-eval-harness.zip) and a short README that describes the measurement definitions we use. Key points for alignment (please confirm / correct):

1) Warm-up: we19ll do a 5 minute warm-up (same as you suggested) but will also run a short run of 1000 scripted requests to prime KV caches before the timed window.
2) Measurement windows: we19ll measure steady-state over a 15-minute window and report p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies plus mean and standard deviation. We19ll also report tail-duration breakdown (>=500ms, >=1s).
3) Throughput: reported as sustained QPS during the steady-state window, and we19ll report max observed instantaneous QPS.
4) Concurrency: we19ll model 50 concurrent streaming connections. Important: we19ll treat each streaming connection as a long-lived TCP/WebSocket session and measure per-chunk latencies as well as end-to-end response completion times.
5) Streaming semantics: harness will surface partial-token timings, bytes-per-chunk, and early-cancel rates.
6) Tokenization: please confirm tokenizer version + vocab you used for prompt-set v1; we default to RedwoodTokenizer-v2.
7) Model mapping: please confirm the exact EdgeFin model variant names you want tested so we map to the correct Redwood runtime image.
8) Resource config: we19ll run initial tests on our dedicated c5-gpu-small (2xA100 equiv) config and can scale to larger pools if needed 14 let us know if you want a single-GPU baseline first.

Proposed timeline: run prelims Oct 5-6, internal review Oct 7, share full writeup Oct 9. If that works, Samir please send keys and a whitelist for the EdgeFin IPs, and confirm tokenizer/model mapping.

Vivek / Dylan 14 can you please review the harness README and confirm we19re capturing GPU counters + per-request trace ids (so EdgeFin can correlate with their traces)?

Thanks!
Marissa

Attachment: redwood-eval-harness.zip

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeFin benchmarking: performance/SLO qualification & methodology exchange

Looping in a couple of implementation notes:

- KV-cache warm-up: do the 1000 scripted requests as Marissa suggested, but also sample a few long-history prompts so we prime large KV entries.
- Concurrency accounting: measure concurrency by active connection id (not by inflight request count) 14 this matches how EdgeFin described it.
- Batch sizing: we19ll run with batch size 1 for streaming paths and a small batching variant (up to 8) for non-streaming to compare efficiency.
- Telemetry: include GPU utilization, GPU power draw, GPU memory high-water mark, and per-step kernel timing (where available). Log trace_id on each request so EdgeFin can cross-reference.
- Reproducibility: record exact Docker image / model SHA and quantization flags in the report.

I19ll prep a short checklist for the bench run and drop into the shared Drive folder.

14Vivek
Sr. Eng Manager, Serving
Vivek@redwood.ai

Perfect 14 thanks for the fast turnaround.

We confirm tokenizer: EdgeFinTokenizer-v3 (I uploaded mapping file to the Drive). Test models: GEN-1.1 and GEN-1.2 (production tags). We19ll send a short IP whitelist and an API key for the run by EOD. Oct 5 schedule works.

Samir
